Louis Pappas Corp vs Mv Kaptan Hasan Onal Imo 9539559 on 26
March, 2024
Author: R.I. Chagla 
Bench: R.I. Chagla
 This Order is modified/corrected by Speaking to Minutes Order dated 0
 3-Sheriff Report
 Kavita S. J.
 In The High Court Of Judicature At Bombay
 Ordinary Original Civil Jurisdiction
 Sheriff'S Report No. 14 Of 2024
 In
 Commercial Admiralty Suit No. 14 Of 2023
 Louis Pappas Corporation ...Pl
 Versus
 Mv Kaptan Hasan Onal (Imo 9539559) ...De
 ----------
 Ms. Bulbul Singh Rajpurohit a/w Mr. Siddharth Manek i/b M/s
 Crawford Bayley & Co. for the Plaintiff. 
 Mr. Prathamesh Kamat a/w Kayush Zaiwalla, Vidhi Mehta i/b
 Shantanu Singh for Applicant (Vessel Agent). 
 Mr. D.S. Choudhari, Deputy Sheriff present. 
 ----------
 Coram : R.I. Chagla, J.
 Dated : 26Th March, 20
 ORDER :
1. The Sheriff's Report is being heard. Arguments have been canvassed by both the sides. 
KAVITA 2. An enquiry had been sought by this Court with regard to SUSHIL JADHAV the E-mail dated 19th February, 2024 addressed by the Deputy Conservator, Mormugau Port Trust ("MPT"),
Goa to the Vessel Agent - This Order is modified/corrected by Speaking to Minutes Order dated 02/04/2024 3-Sheriff Report 14.24 in COMAS 14.2023.doc M/s Joanes P and Company ("the Applicant"). This has been completed by the Deputy Conservator, MPT, Goa furnishing their Louis Pappas Corp vs Mv Kaptan Hasan Onal Imo 9539559 on 26 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99541864/
1 response and also remaining present on the previous date i.e. 15 th March, 2024. It was noted on that date that according to the Deputy Conservator, MPT, Goa, the subject Vessel was considered to be abandoned with effect from 27 th May, 2023. This has also been mentioned in the communication dated 13 th March, 2024 addressed by the Deputy Conservator, MPT, Goa to the Sheriff of Mumbai. 
3. Pursuant to the directions of this Court, the Applicant and the Plaintiff have filed their respective Written Submissions. 
4. Mr. Shyam Kapadia, learned Counsel appearing for the Plaintiff has submitted that the above Sheriff's Report has been filed upon considering a praecipe and compilation of documents filed alongwith the praecipe by the Applicant on 20 th February, 2024. The praecipe sought directions that the expenses purportedly incurred by the Applicant towards supply of provisions during a certain period after the arrest order be treated as Sheriff's expenses and reimbursed out of sale proceeds on priority. He has submitted that by the said praecipe the Applicant had submitted seven Tax Invoices, all dated 1 st This Order is modified/corrected by Speaking to Minutes Order dated 02/04/2024 3-Sheriff Report 14.24 in COMAS 14.2023.doc February, 2024, totaling Rs.52,41,143/-
for supplies made to the Defendant-Vessel in June, July and August 2023. Notably, the Sheriff's Report considers only five (of the seven) Invoices and states that this Court has considered the claim of Rs.47,44,041/- made by the Applicant for supplies made to be paid from the sale proceeds.
Importantly, there is no finding / statement / suggestion from the Sheriff that the said expenses were in the nature of Sheriff's expenses. There were no instructions given by the Sheriff to make the subject supplies; nor were the supplies or payments routed through the Sheriff's office. 
5. Mr. Shyam Kapadia has further submitted that this Court had directed the Deputy Conservator,
MPT, Goa to submit its response as to when the subject Vessel was abandoned and in particular identify when the inspection of Defendant's subject Vessel was carried out by the concerned authorities and when the direction was issued to the Applicant to supply provisions, fresh water and garbage disposal as has been mentioned in the E-mail dated 19 th February, 2024 addressed by the Deputy Conservator, MPT, Goa to the Applicant. He has submitted that the Deputy Conservator,
MPT, Goa has mentioned in its Letter dated 13th March, 2024 addressed to the This Order is modified/corrected by Speaking to Minutes Order dated 02/04/2024 3-Sheriff Report 14.24 in COMAS 14.2023.doc Sheriff's office which has been placed on record through Sheriff's Report No.20 of 2024 that according to the Deputy Conservator the subject Vessel was abandoned as on 27 th May, 2023. This is on the premise that the Deputy Conservator had demanded payment of outstanding dues from the Owners of the Defendant-Vessel on 5 th May, 2023. The Owners of the subject Vessel in their response (which was received by MPT on 12th May, 2023) had sought 15 days'
time to clear the dues. Their request was favourable considered by MPT. However, since Owners failed to clear the outstanding port dues within the 15 day's extension granted by MPT, the Deputy Conservator of MPT, Goa stated that the subject Vessel was abandoned on 27th May, 2023. 
6. Mr. Shyam Kapadia has submitted that notably the 27 th May, 2023 was even prior to the arrest of the subject Vessel on 31 st May, 2023. He has submitted that mere failure to pay the Port dues on the extended date for payment is not a ground of abandonment recognized by the Division Bench of Louis Pappas Corp vs Mv Kaptan Hasan Onal Imo 9539559 on 26 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99541864/
2 this Court in The Swedish Club Vs. V8 Pool Inc., & Other 1. He has submitted that the MPT Goa's view on when 'abandonment' occurs cannot override the settle 1 Commercial Appeal No.108/2021 in Interim Appln. No.2062/2021 dtd.23/03/2022 This Order is modified/corrected by Speaking to Minutes Order dated 02/04/2024 3-Sheriff Report 14.24 in COMAS 14.2023.doc law on this aspect. 
He has submitted that if every time a Vessel fails to pay port dues, it is deemed to be 'abandonment'
it would lead to a chaotic and practically anarchic situation. The consequences of 'abandonment' of a Vessel are dire and, it is for this reason, that this Court has thought fit to detail various different situations where a Vessel can be deemed to be 'abandoned'. 
7. Mr. Shyam Kapadia has submitted that the Deputy Conservator has not identified the date of inspection or the date of instructions in his E-mail dated 19th February, 2024 and instead stated that "it is a routine for the undersigned to take rounds of the port.... for safeguard of all the crafts in the port" and "the Vessel Agent was verbally instructed to give all support to the Vessel crew as it was found that the ships crew were morally down due to the negligence of the Owners." He has submitted that despite explicit orders of this Court, the Deputy Conservator fails to identify these timelines. He has submitted that in order to qualify as Sheriff's expenses, the expenses are required to be made at the instance of the Sheriff or this Court and to be routed through the office of the Sheriff. All these safeguards cannot simply be bypassed by suggesting that the Deputy Conservator at an indeterminate time, through oral instructions, This Order is modified/corrected by Speaking to Minutes Order dated 02/04/2024 3-Sheriff Report 14.24 in COMAS 14.2023.doc instructed the Applicant to make the supplies. 
8. Mr. Shyam Kapadia has submitted that the Owners of the Defendant-Vessel have filed their appearance in the present proceedings and confirmed that supplies were made to the subject Vessel till 18th August, 2023. The Delivery Challans submitted by the Applicant are for the period from June 2023 till August 2023. It is an admitted position that even when the subject Vessel was under arrest, the Owner of the subject Vessel was responsible for maintaining the subject Vessel and crew on board. At the relevant time, the Applicant was taking instructions from Owners of the Defendant-Vessel for supplying provisions to the Defendant-Vessel/Crew. 
9. Mr. Shyam Kapadia has submitted that in the Orders dated 12th October, 2023 and 20th October,
2023 it is recorded that the Owners of the Defendant - Vessel supplied provisions to the Defendant-Vessel till 18 th August, 2023. He has submitted that to now suggest that these supplies were made to the credit of the Sheriff would be to overreach the position recorded and accepted by this Court. Resultantly, the subject supplies by the Applicant were made pursuant to instructions from the Owners and This Order is modified/corrected by Speaking to Minutes Order dated 02/04/2024 3-Sheriff Report 14.24 in COMAS 14.2023.doc were to the account of / credit of the Owners of the Defendant-Vessel. Therefore, ipso facto, the same cannot be treated as Sheriff's expenses. 
10. Mr. Shyam Kapadia has submitted that in the said Order dated 12th October, 2023, it has been recorded that the Owners supplied provisions and necessaries regularly until 18 th August, 2023. 
Further, the said order records that in the event Owners fail to arrange for subsequent supplies, the Sheriff was to request the Shipping Agent to make supplies at the expense of the Owner of the Louis Pappas Corp vs Mv Kaptan Hasan Onal Imo 9539559 on 26 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99541864/
3 Defendant-Vessel. He has submitted that a reading of the order makes it clear that the supplies made until 18th August, 2023 were to the credit of the Owner and not the Sheriff; and if further supplies were required, the Sheriff was to commission the same being provided. In fact, all supplies thereafter have been treated as Sheriff's expenses and paid to the Applicant. It cannot allow the Applicant to convert its claim against the Owners for prior supplies into claims against the Sheriff and be paid in priority. 
11. Mr. Shyam Kapadia has also referred to the subsequent Order dated 20th October, 2023,
wherein it is recorded that in case of This Order is modified/corrected by Speaking to Minutes Order dated 02/04/2024 3-Sheriff Report 14.24 in COMAS 14.2023.doc fresh supplies provided by the Vessel Agent at the request of Deputy Sheriff, the expenses incurred shall be borne by the Defendant. It is specifically mentioned therein that supplies had not been provided by the Defendant to the on board crew members since last supplies on 18th August, 2023. It is further recorded that the expenses of the Sheriff incurred for fresh supplies and for which request is to be made to the Shipping Agent to provide the fresh supplies to the on board crew members, these expenses shall be borne by the Defendant. This shall continue to operate till the next date of hearing. 
12. Mr. Shyam Kapadia has submitted that this Court had acknowledged that the Defendant Owner had made supplies to the Defendant-Vessel until 18th August, 2023 and the supplies were made through the Applicant, their local agents. Thus, they were made at the instance of and to the credit of the Owners; not the Sheriff.
13. Mr. Shyam Kapadia has submitted that in an Affidavit dated 25th September, 2023 filed by Owners of the Defendant - Vessel in response to the Sheriff's Report No.53 of 2023, it is mentioned that the Owners have made various payments to Mr. Glorio Fernandes of Applicant on 24th July,
2023 and 27th July, 2023. The said payments This Order is modified/corrected by Speaking to Minutes Order dated 02/04/2024 3-Sheriff Report 14.24 in COMAS 14.2023.doc were made to the Applicant by the Owners of the Defendant-Vessel during the time which they are now claiming as Sheriff's expenses. There is no denial of the fact that the Owner made these payments. Even assuming that these were only part-payments and substantial amounts are still due to the Applicant - they are due from the Owners, for which the Applicant is required to file appropriate proceedings and be paid out in the priorities prescribed under the Act. It cannot leapfrog other creditors by shifting its counterparty from the Owner to the Sheriff. 
14. Mr. Shyam Kapadia has submitted that in view of the said orders of this Court and the Affidavit filed by the Defendant Owner, it is clear that the Owners of the Defendant-Vessel had supplied provisions, fresh water and garbage disposal until at least 18th August, 2023. These may have been done through their local Agent (the Applicant) but the Owners were responsible for making payments in respect thereof; not the Sheriff. 
15. Mr. Shyam Kapadia has submitted that the expenses incurred without sanction of the Admiralty Court cannot be treated as Sheriff's expenses. A party wishing to rank an expense incurred by This Order is modified/corrected by Speaking to Minutes Order dated 02/04/2024 3-Sheriff Report 14.24 in COMAS 14.2023.doc it in connection with the safety, preservation and maintenance of a Louis Pappas Corp vs Mv Kaptan Hasan Onal Imo 9539559 on 26 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99541864/
4 Vessel under arrest as Sheriff's expenses is obliged to seek prior sanction and/or approval of the Court or the Sheriff to enjoy a higher priority in the distribution of proceeds of a judicial sale of the Vessel. It is absurd to suggest that all expenses incurred post-arrest of a Vessel are Sheriff's expenses; and, in fairness to the advocates of the Applicant, even they have not canvassed such an extreme proposition. 
16. Mr. Shyam Kapadia has relied upon the decision of this Court in Swedish Club (supra), wherein detailed guidelines have been passed by the Division Bench of this Court after considering Rule 1084 of the Bombay High Court (Original Side) Rules on when expenses can be treated as Sheriff's expenses. A comparative chart of Swedish Club Judgment has been annexed at Annexure-A to the written submission of the Plaintiff. 
17. Mr. Shyam Kapadia has submitted that upon perusal of the comparative chart, it is clear that none of the guidelines laid down by the Division Bench of this Court in the Swedish Club Judgment has been followed in the present case. 
This Order is modified/corrected by Speaking to Minutes Order dated 02/04/2024 3-Sheriff Report 14.24 in COMAS 14.2023.doc 18. Mr. Shyam Kapadia has submitted that the Applicant had placed reliance on the decision of this Court in Irwin Edmund Sequeira and Ors. Vs. MV Karnika (IMO No.8521220) 2 and of the Singapore Court in "The Nagasaki Spirit" 3 and "Aquarius III" which considers the question as to whether the expenses incurred without prior sanction of the Sheriff can be treated as Sheriff's expenses. It has been held in those cases that the Admiralty Court has wide discretion in balancing equities in a proper case and that the expenses may be treated as Sheriff's expenses even post-facto. 
He has submitted that it is pertinent to note that in both the cases the claim related to expenses incurred after the Court held that the Owners abandoned the Vessels. 
19. Mr. Shyam Kapadia has placed reliance upon decision of the Singapore Court in The Makassar Caraka Jaya Niaga III 39 4 which considered the aforementioned decisions of the Singapore Court and upon so considering confirmed that abandonment of the Vessel by Owners and prior sanction by Court / Sheriff is a sine qua non for an Agent's expenses to be treated as Sheriff's expenses. He has particularly relied upon Paragraph 50 of the said decision. He 2 IA(L) No.2893/2021 in COMAS(L)No.5166/2020 3 1994 SGHC 115 4 2012 SGHC 175 This Order is modified/corrected by Speaking to Minutes Order dated 02/04/2024 3-Sheriff Report 14.24 in COMAS 14.2023.doc has submitted that in the present case as in the Makassar (supra), the subject Vessel was not abandoned by the Owners of the subject Vessel. They repeatedly appeared in proceedings before this Court and in fact provided supplies till 18 th August, 2023 as recorded in orders passed by this Court. The Owners have also placed evidence of making payments to the agents of the Defendant-Vessel for supply of provisions during the relevant period. Even if these were part- payments, the balance due to the Applicant is from the Owner (for which it can file proceedings like other creditors); not the Sheriff. 
Louis Pappas Corp vs Mv Kaptan Hasan Onal Imo 9539559 on 26 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99541864/
5 20. Mr. Shyam Kapadia has submitted that the expenses of the Applicant in the praecipe filed cannot be treated as Sheriff's expenses for the period June-August 2023 i.e. prior to 18 th August,
2023. The Applicant is required to file an independent Suit for its claims and is not left without redress. No prejudice will be caused to the Applicant as their right to approach this Court and make a claim against the sale proceeds remains. 
21. Mr. Shyam Kapadia has submitted that undoubtedly this Court has wide discretion. However, it ought not to ignore the established principles for treating expenses as Sheriff's expenses. He This Order is modified/corrected by Speaking to Minutes Order dated 02/04/2024 3-Sheriff Report 14.24 in COMAS 14.2023.doc has submitted that in view of non-abandonment of the Defendant- Vessel during the relevant time and atleast until 18 th August, 2023, as borne out from the orders of this Court, this Court ought not to have the Applicant's expenses treated as Sheriff's expenses as the same would operate to seriously dilute the principles of Sheriff's expenses. Further, to proceed as MPT Goa suggests and treat a Vessel as abandoned upon non-payment of Port dues would be contrary to the settled and detailed guidelines in the Swedish Club Judgment. Accordingly, the Applicant's claim as Sheriff's expenses is required to be rejected and the Applicant be remanded to file an appropriate Suit for its claim like all other unpaid creditors of the Owners of the Defendant-Vessel. 
22. Mr. Prathamesh Kamat, learned Counsel appearing for the Applicant-M/s Joanes P and Company has submitted that the objection taken by the Plaintiff with regard to the Applicant not being entitled to seek directions on a praecipe is a hyper technical objection and that too, is entirely misplaced. The Application for treating expenses of the Applicant as Sheriff's expenses is being considered on the Sheriff's Report which has sought the directions and no longer on the praecipe of the Applicant. Further, the praecipe of the This Order is modified/corrected by Speaking to Minutes Order dated 02/04/2024 3-Sheriff Report 14.24 in COMAS 14.2023.doc Applicant as well as documents are now a part of the Sheriff's Report. 
23. Mr. Prathamesh Kamat has submitted that the Admiralty Court has power to declare expenses as Sheriff's expenses even if the same are incurred without the prior permission of the Court. He has referred to the relevant Rule 1084 of the Bombay High Court (Original side) Rules, 1980 ("Rules").
He has submitted that upon a reading of the said Rule, it is clear that all expenses are required to be incurred for the safety and preservation of the Vessel and its crew during the period the Vessel remains under arrest shall be treated as Sheriff's expenses. What is important is the expenses that are incurred are (i) incurred post arrest; (ii) are incurred either for the safety and preservation of the Vessel or its crew during arrest. 
24. Mr. Kamat has submitted that it is important to note that when the Vessel is arrested, the crew (as per the safe manning requirements) have to be on board the Vessel. The Vessel cannot be left unmanned as it can pose a threat to life, property, environment. The manning ensures safety of the Vessel as well as property and people around the Vessel. Therefore, it is essential that the crew which remains on board the Vessel is provided with basic requirement This Order is modified/corrected by Speaking to Minutes Order dated 02/04/2024 3-Sheriff Report 14.24 in COMAS 14.2023.doc of food, water and other essentials which are essential for their survival on Louis Pappas Corp vs Mv Kaptan Hasan Onal Imo 9539559 on 26 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99541864/
6 board the Vessel. 
25. Mr. Kamat has submitted that though it is ideal that the party who incurs expenses post arrest and would want to treat such expenses as Sheriff's expenses, must take prior leave of the Admiralty Court. However, absence of such a leave cannot be treated as fatal to the claim of a person who supplies necessaries to the Vessel and the crew post arrest, in all situations. The Admiralty Court is not precluded from declaring such expenses by a person without its leave as Sheriff's expenses. 
26. Mr. Kamat has submitted that the Plaintiff has based its oppositions on the guidelines laid down by the Division Bench of this Court in Swedish Club (supra). This opposition is without any substance. The guidelines laid down in Swedish Club Judgment cannot be treated as an absolute proposition of law which would impose fetters on the Admiralty Court from treating certain expenses without its leave for the sustenance of the crew on board the Vessel as Sheriff's expenses. 
27. Mr. Kamat has submitted that all progressive countries This Order is modified/corrected by Speaking to Minutes Order dated 02/04/2024 3-Sheriff Report 14.24 in COMAS 14.2023.doc including India have interpreted that an Admiralty Court does retain its powers to treat expenses which were incurred without the prior approval of the Admiralty Court as Sheriff's expenses. 
However, this can be done as long as such expenses are incurred to ensure survival of the crew on board the said Vessel which is under arrest under the orders of the Admiralty Court. He has placed reliance upon the Judgments of Singapore Court in Nagasaki Spirit (supra) at Paragraphs 16 to 19,
28, 29, 32, Aquarius III (supra) at Paragraphs 49 to 51 and Irwin Edmund Sequeira (supra) passed in Interim Application (L) No.2893 of 2021 in Commercial Admiralty Suit (L) No.5166 of 2020 passed on 17 th & 18th January, 2023 at Paragraphs 35, 39, 42 to 46.
28. Mr. Kamat has submitted that on a reading of the aforesaid Judgments, more particularly, the Judgment in M.V. Karnika (supra) (which considers the Judgment of Swedish Club (supra) ), it has been clearly held that in a given case, having regard to the exigencies of the situation, where supply of provisions and necessaries is imperative to ensure the survival of the Vessel and the crew, the Court retains the jurisdiction to direct such expenses, even if incurred without its approval, be treated as Sheriff's expenses. This Order is modified/corrected by Speaking to Minutes Order dated 02/04/2024 3-Sheriff Report 14.24 in COMAS 14.2023.doc 29. Mr. Kamat has submitted that the the opposition of the Plaintiff on the ground that no prior approval of the Court or Sheriff was taken as the reason for rejection of the expenses incurred by the Applicant, is liable to be rejected. 
30. Mr. Kamat has submitted that the Plaintiff has merely placed reliance upon the prior Orders dated 12th October, 2023 and 20th October, 2023, to suggest that supplies made upto 18th August,
2023, were to the credit of the Owner. This overlooks not just the documents produced alongwith the Sheriff's Report but also the communication addressed by the Deputy Conservator of the MPT,
Goa as well as the oral submissions before this Court on 15th March, 2023. He has submitted that the Deputy Conservator of MPT, Goa in its communication dated 13th March, 2023 to the Deputy Sheriff has categorically stated that the subject Vessel is treated as abandoned by its Owner with Louis Pappas Corp vs Mv Kaptan Hasan Onal Imo 9539559 on 26 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99541864/
7 effect from 27th May, 2023. This, on account of the Owners not taking any action or showing any interest in their asset despite repeated directions issued to the Applicant to take care with respect to supply of food, water, medical needs, repatriation of crew.
31. Mr. Kamat has submitted that the aforementioned This Order is modified/corrected by Speaking to Minutes Order dated 02/04/2024 3-Sheriff Report 14.24 in COMAS 14.2023.doc directions were issued by the Deputy Conservator of MPT, Goa as there was warning of a Cyclonic Storm "Biparjoy"
formed over the Arabian Sea and due to which the weather had deteriorated. The Port Authorities had further given direction to the Applicant to deploy a tug alongside the Defendant-Vessel. This was also communicated by the Vessel Agent to the Owner of the Defendant-Vessel vide E-mail dated 5th June, 2023. However, the said E-mail did not accord any reply from the Owner of the Defendant-Vessel and thus, MPT, Goa considered there to be an act of abandonment by the Defendant- Vessel's Owner. 
32. Mr. Kamat has submitted that the Deputy Conservator, MPT, Goa in response to the oral query of this Court, clarified that ever since May 2023, despite directions of the Deputy Conservator, the Owner failed to provide supplies of fresh water, food and other necessaries. It is for this reason,
MPT, Goa, treated the Defendant- Vessel to have been abandoned by the Owners. Further, the Deputy Conservator had around 1st June, 2023 directed the Applicant to supply food, fresh water and other necessities. Thus, the supplies made by the Applicant on 6 th June, 2023, was clearly to ensure that the crew on board the Defendant-vessel survives and who can This Order is modified/corrected by Speaking to Minutes Order dated 02/04/2024 3-Sheriff Report 14.24 in COMAS 14.2023.doc accordingly man the Vessel. Thus, the contention that the supply was to the credit of the Owners is entirely misplaced and the expenses ought to be treated as Sheriff's expenses. 
33. Mr. Kamat has submitted that when the said Orders dated 12th October, 2023 and 20th October,
2023 were passed by this Court, neither the Applicant nor the Deputy Conservator of MPT, Goa was before this Court to explain the ground reality. 
34. Mr. Kamat has submitted that the conduct of the Owners of the Defendant-Vessel being less than wholesome is now writ large on the record of this Court. A statutory body such as the Port Trust who is at the site and is aware of ground realities faced by the crew on board the said vessel is now brought on record before this Court. In such a scenario, it is imperative that the version of the Port which is in sync with the version of the Applicant, is believed. 
35. Mr. Kamat has distinguished the Judgment of Singapore Court in The Makassar Caraka Jaya Niaga III 39 (supra). That case did not face a situation where the Deputy Conservator of the Port had requested the Agent to supply food, fresh water and necessaries to the crew. Like in the present case, the Singapore case did not deal This Order is modified/corrected by Speaking to Minutes Order dated 02/04/2024 3-Sheriff Report 14.24 in COMAS 14.2023.doc with a situation where during storm the Owners went incommunicado forcing the Port to contact the Agents. The said Judgment cannot be of any assistance to the Plaintiff. 
Louis Pappas Corp vs Mv Kaptan Hasan Onal Imo 9539559 on 26 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99541864/
8 36. Mr. Kamat has submitted that the miniscule payment made by the Owners, months after abandonment does not amount to recall of the abandonment. He has submitted that the amount paid by one Dhananjay Singh, Director of Mahadeva Shipping & Management Private Limited was from the manning agent of the Defendant-Vessel. This payment has been relied upon in the Affidavit dated 25th September, 2023 filed by the Owner in Sheriff's Report No.53 of 2023. The said monies were not paid by the Owners and this payment has already been factored in Paragraph 3 of the present Sheriff's Report. The said amounts are deducted form the entitlement of the Applicant. 
37. Mr. Kamat has submitted that it would be catastrophic to treat miniscule payment made months after as a reversal of the act of abandonment by the Owner. It is like putting a premium over the default of the Owner and putting parties who have actually stepped in to help the crew on directions of statutory authorities as detriment. This Order is modified/corrected by Speaking to Minutes Order dated 02/04/2024 3-Sheriff Report 14.24 in COMAS 14.2023.doc It is settled law that the Courts do not accept an interpretation which results in absurdity. On this ground also, the objection of the Plaintiff is liable to be rejected. Accordingly, the Sheriff's Report be allowed and be made absolute directing a sum of Rs.47,44,041/- to be paid to the Applicant as Sheriff's expenses. 
38. Having considered the submissions, there appears to be a reliance placed by the Plaintiff on two prior Orders dated 12 th October, 2023 and 20th October, 2023 passed by this Court to contend that supplies were made by the Owners of the Defendant-Vessel upto 18th August, 2023 and hence these can be no abandonment of the Vessel prior thereto. The said orders appear to be the basis for the Plaintiff's opposition to the present Application. The Plaintiff's contention being that the expenses having been incurred by the Applicant for the months of June, July and August i.e. prior to 18 th August, 2023, they cannot be treated as the Sheriff's expenses. A heavy reliance has been placed by the Plaintiff on the decision of the Division Bench in Swedish Club (supra).
39. It is relevant to note that the said orders dated 12 th October, 2023 and 20th October 2023 were passed by this Court This Order is modified/corrected by Speaking to Minutes Order dated 02/04/2024 3-Sheriff Report 14.24 in COMAS 14.2023.doc merely upon the submissions of the Owners of the Defendant-Vessel and without taking into account the material facts which have come to light upon this Court directing the Deputy Conservator of MPT, Goa to give its say and also to remain present in the Court for clarifying as to when according to him was the Defendant-Vessel abandoned. These directions were issued in view of the communication addressed by the Deputy Sheriff, wherein it was stated that during the inspection of the Defendant-Vessel the crew members expressed their grievance for non-supply of provisions, fresh water and garbage disposal. The Deputy Conservator had accordingly ordered the Applicant to supply provisions, fresh water and for garbage disposal. This being the necessaries as per the Merchant Shipping Act, the crew was entitled for the same. This communication is as and by way of E-mail dated 19 th February, 2024 sent by the Deputy Conservator of MPT, Goa to the Deputy Sheriff and which is part of the present Sheriff's Report. 
40. Thereafter, the Deputy Conservator of MPT, Goa has appeared before this Court and given its say as well as addressed a letter dated 13th March, 2023 to the Deputy Sheriff, wherein the Deputy Conservator has stated that the Defendant-Vessel may be This Order is modified/corrected by Louis Pappas Corp vs Mv Kaptan Hasan Onal Imo 9539559 on 26 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99541864/
9 Speaking to Minutes Order dated 02/04/2024 3-Sheriff Report 14.24 in COMAS 14.2023.doc considered as abandoned with effect from 27th May, 2023.
41. On the prior dates, when this Court had passed the aforementioned orders relied upon by the Plaintiff, this Court was not apprised of the fact that the directions were issued by Deputy Conservator of MPT, Goa at a time when the weather had deteriorated on account of a severe cyclonic storm "Biparjoy" which was formed over the Arabian Sea. Further, it became essential to protect the Defendant-Vessel by deploying a tug alongside the Defendant-Vessel and for safeguarding the crew members who were on board of the Defendant-Vessel by the provision of necessaries which were imperative to ensure their survival. The Owners of the Defendant-Vessel were intimated about the same by the Vessel Agent who in turn was the recipient of the directions. 
However, the Owner of the Defendant-Vessel failed to respond to the same. Thus, it was treated by as an act of abandonment. Had these factors come to light, this Court would not have recorded in the prior Orders that the Owner had supplied provisions and necessaries regularly until 18 th August, 2023 and / or that the last supplies were made by the Owners of the Defendant-Vessel on 18th August, 2023. I thus find no merit in the submission of Mr. Shyam Kapadia that the Defendant- This Order is modified/corrected by Speaking to Minutes Order dated 02/04/2024 3-Sheriff Report 14.24 in COMAS 14.2023.doc Vessel cannot be stated to have been abandoned prior to 18 th August,
2023.
42. This Court has laid down guidelines in Swedish Club (supra) as to when a Vessel can be stated to have been abandoned. These guidelines have been heavily relied upon by Mr. Shyam Kapadia on behalf of the Plaintiff by drawing a comparison of the present case with these guidelines to show that these guidelines have not been met. However, the Division Bench of this Court by laying down these guidelines in Swedish Club (supra) has held in Paragraph 51 of the decision that these are only guidelines and that the Admiralty Court is at liberty to use its discretion in any given case. Thus,
these guidelines cannot impose fetters on the Admiralty Court from treating certain expenses without its leave for the sustenance of the crew on board the subject Vessel as Sheriff's expenses. 
43. The decisions of the Singapore Court relied upon by Mr. Prathamesh Kamat on behalf of the Applicant viz.
